intro: Tests correct use of past perfect and present perfect in context

items.q: By the time the film started, we ___ our popcorn already.
items.why: Past perfect shows action completed before another past event.

items.q: I can't find my keys. I think I ___ them somewhere.
items.why: Present perfect links a past action to a present situation.

items.q: She ___ never visited a foreign country before that trip.
items.why: Past perfect with 'before that trip' refers to experience up to a past point.

items.q: We ___ just finished dinner when the guests arrived.
items.why: Past perfect shows the meal ended just before another past event.

items.q: He looks tired because he ___ been working all day.
items.why: Present perfect explains a present result of a recent past action.

parts.title: Complete the sentences with the correct form.

items.post: already, so I wasn't hungry at the restaurant.
items.why: Past perfect shows eating was completed before the past restaurant visit.

items.post: in three different countries since she finished university.
items.why: Present perfect with 'since' connects past experience to the present.

items.pre: When I arrived at the station, the train
items.why: Past perfect shows the train left before the speaker arrived.

items.post: sushi before they went to Japan last year.
items.why: Past perfect shows zero experience before a specific past point.

items.post: you the document, so please check your email.
items.why: Present perfect with 'just' describes a very recent action with present relevance.

items.pre: By the time he was thirty, he
items.why: Past perfect describes an action completed before a past deadline.

parts.title: Find and correct the mistake in each sentence.

items.sentence: I have finished my homework before my mum called me for dinner.
items.corrected: I had finished my homework before my mum called me for dinner.
items.why: Past perfect needed; the homework was done before another past event.

items.sentence: She had never seen that actor before, but she had heard of him.
items.corrected: She had never seen that actor before, but she has heard of him.
items.why: Present perfect needed; she still knows him now, linking past to present.

items.sentence: We have already left the house when it started to snow.
items.corrected: We had already left the house when it started to snow.
items.why: Past perfect needed; leaving happened before another completed past event.

parts.title: Write your own sentences.
parts.pointsLabel: 2 points: 1 for correct form, 1 for meaning and use

items.prompt: Write one sentence about a skill or activity you have learned or tried for the first time in your life so far.
items.criteria: Accept any grammatically correct sentence using present perfect, e.g. 'I have never ridden a horse' or 'I have always wanted to learn Spanish'.
items.example: I have always wanted to learn how to play the guitar.

items.prompt: Write one sentence describing something you had already done before an important event in your past, for example before starting school or before moving to a ne
items.criteria: Accept any grammatically correct sentence using past perfect before or alongside a simple past event.
items.example: I had already learned to read before I started primary school.
